commons.title: Shariff Kabunsuan Festival 2016 Guinakit Fluvial Parade 4.jpg
commons.description:
Among the highlights of Shariff Kabunsuan Festival 2016 Celebration is the Guinakit Fluvial Parade jointly conducted on December 19, 2016 at Cotabato City Wharf, by the Department of Tourism-ARMM, Department of Tourism- RO XII, and City Government.  Guinakit Fluvial Parade is a display of colorfully decorated tandem-bancas or ‘guinakit’ commemorating the arrival of Arab Missionary Shariff Kabunsuan who introduced Islam in Mindanao in the 16th Century.
Shariff Kabunsuan Festival is a celebration of Islam and display of Muslim religion and culture.
commons.editorial_reason: Caption ties the decorated guinakit parade to the Shariff Kabunsuan Festival and Muslim culture in Mindanao; the image shows decorated traditional boats.

commons.title: Kulintang 07.jpg
commons.description: The eight Philippine horizontally laid, knobbed gongs known as the kulintang used as a main melodic instrument in the kulintang ensemble.  Here, it is used as an accompaniment for a healing ritual. The dancers perform the dance, sagayan, while the kulintang player performs the piece, Taggungo.
commons.editorial_reason: The caption describes a Philippine kulintang healing ritual but does not specifically attribute the pictured performers or practice to the Maguindanao people.
